items.title: Virginia Mayhew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2022
items.q: You know I sent him a message immediately because for two reasons. First of all he totally gets it

ctx.x: Okay. It says, “With few guarantees of either recognition or fortune, the life of a serious jazz instrumentalist is a saga of fortitude. Virginia Mayhew, a post-bop saxophonist and composer of obvious depth and feeling has bobbed and weaved through the musical trenches for four decades now, accruing respect from her peers and offering pleasure to those who have become acquainted with her artistry.” And then it goes on to say your upcoming gig at Small’s, which “helps keep the heart of mainstream jazz beating,…

Wow. You know I sent him a message immediately because for two reasons. First of all he totally gets it, and second of all because all the years that I’ve been here I’ve never gotten mentioned in the New Yorker. And it’s like, it’s not really a big deal obviously but I was so happy. And I have a friend who’s 94 and she gets the New Yorker and she’s always reading it, and finally she saw my name there with a good little blurb so it was wonderful on so many levels.
I hope you cut it out, because I would have.
